how-to-choose-cctv-cameras.title: How to Choose the Right CCTV Cameras for Your Facility
how-to-choose-cctv-cameras.description: A practical guide to choosing CCTV cameras: where to mount them, resolution, lighting, and recording. Know the right questions before you ask for a quote.
how-to-choose-cctv-cameras.keywords: how to choose CCTV cameras, CCTV buying guide, security camera guide, CCTV Makkah
how-to-choose-cctv-cameras.excerpt: Before asking about price, know which camera type suits your site, where it should be mounted, and how many days you need to keep recordings.

blocks.p: Choosing CCTV cameras does not start with the device itself. It starts with understanding the place you want to protect. The right camera for a shop entrance is not necessarily the right one for a parking lot or a large warehouse.

blocks.h2: Start with the purpose of monitoring

blocks.p: Do you need monitoring as a deterrent only? To document events? Or to follow daily operations? Each purpose determines the camera type, its angle, and where it goes.

ul: Entrances and exits: you need clear coverage of faces and vehicle plates.
Point of sale and cash areas: you need high detail and an angle that shows what happens.
Corridors and parking: you need wide coverage with fewer cameras.
Warehouses: you need good night vision and coverage of aisles between shelves.

blocks.p: Higher resolution means finer detail, but it also increases recording size and storage needs. Do not choose the highest resolution for every point; choose it according to distance and purpose. Lighting matters too: a good camera in very low light may not show anything useful without night vision or supplementary lighting.

blocks.tip: Tip: before buying, ask for a site survey. A survey reveals blocked angles, real lighting, and distances. It is more accurate than any written specification.

blocks.p: IP cameras suit facilities that need flexibility for expansion and remote viewing. Analog cameras are economical for small projects. Read our article comparing IP and analog cameras for the details.

ul: What angle and distance does each camera cover on my site?
How many days will the system keep recordings with the proposed setup?
Can I add cameras later without replacing the main recorder?
Who maintains the system after installation, and what is the warranty period?

ip-vs-analog-cameras.title: IP Cameras vs Analog Cameras: What Is the Difference?
ip-vs-analog-cameras.description: A clear comparison of IP and analog CCTV cameras in terms of quality, cost, installation, and scalability, so you can choose the right one for your project.
ip-vs-analog-cameras.keywords: IP cameras, analog cameras, IP vs analog cameras, IP CCTV cameras
ip-vs-analog-cameras.excerpt: IP or analog? When to choose each type, and what should really drive the decision for your project.

blocks.p: One of the most common questions we hear is whether to choose IP cameras or analog ones. The answer depends on the size of the project and the flexibility you need, not on which is newer.
IP cameras send video digitally over a data network and record it on an NVR. Analog cameras send video over dedicated cable to a DVR, which converts and records it.

ul: Resolution: IP cameras generally offer higher resolution and a wider range of options.
Scalability: adding an IP camera means extending the network and connecting it to the recorder, which suits large projects well.
Initial cost: analog is often cheaper for small projects with a limited number of points.
Remote viewing: IP cameras make remote monitoring from a phone or another location easier, depending on setup.
Infrastructure: IP needs a good network, while analog needs dedicated cabling.

blocks.tip: Note: the real cost is not only the price of the camera. It includes installation, future expansion, and maintenance. Sometimes the cheapest solution at the start becomes the most expensive over time.

blocks.p: If you have multiple branches, plan to expand, or want higher detail and flexible monitoring, IP cameras are usually the better choice.
If the project is small, the number of points is limited, and the building already has usable analog cabling, analog can be a practical and economical solution.
There is no single answer for everyone. We prefer to survey the site first, then recommend the right type for each area. In some facilities the best solution is a mix of both.

cctv-retention-period.title: How Many Days Should CCTV Recordings Be Kept?
cctv-retention-period.description: The factors that determine how long CCTV recordings should be kept, and how to calculate the storage capacity needed for your recorder.
cctv-retention-period.keywords: CCTV recording retention, CCTV storage capacity, NVR storage, how long to keep camera recordings
cctv-retention-period.excerpt: Retention is not a fixed number for every facility. Learn the factors that affect it and how to calculate the storage you need.

blocks.p: When installing a surveillance system, many people ask: how many days are recordings kept? The answer depends on the purpose of monitoring, the number of cameras, recording quality, and the storage available.

ul: Purpose of monitoring: daily deterrence needs less time than documenting events or looking back at past incidents.
Activity or sector requirements: some sectors have specific retention requirements, which should be confirmed with the relevant authority.
Number and type of cameras: each camera uses storage according to its resolution and frame rate.
Recording mode: continuous recording uses far more storage than motion-triggered recording.
Video compression: compression settings directly affect file size and image quality.

blocks.p: The required storage is roughly: number of cameras × daily recording size per camera × number of retention days. The daily size depends on resolution, frame rate, compression type, and the share of continuous recording.

blocks.tip: Tip: do not calculate using only the maximum case. Add a margin for future changes, and confirm the recorder supports the drive capacity you plan to use.

ul: Buying a larger drive without checking it is compatible with the recorder.
Setting high resolution for every camera, even those that do not need fine detail.
Not reviewing storage after a while, so the disk fills up without warning.
Not checking the device date and time, which makes searching recordings later harder.

blocks.p: If you are not sure of the right numbers for your facility, our team includes the storage calculation in the site survey and explains the options with figures before implementation.

why-cctv-maintenance-matters.title: Why Do CCTV Cameras Need Regular Maintenance?
why-cctv-maintenance-matters.description: The main reasons CCTV cameras need periodic maintenance, what is checked during a visit, and how it reduces sudden faults and losses.
why-cctv-maintenance-matters.keywords: CCTV maintenance, periodic maintenance CCTV, security system maintenance, camera maintenance contract
why-cctv-maintenance-matters.excerpt: A stopped camera means an unmonitored area. Learn what regular maintenance covers, and why it costs less than emergency repairs.

blocks.p: Many people install a surveillance system and then forget it until they need it. When an incident or theft happens, they discover that a camera has been offline for weeks. Regular maintenance prevents this situation.

ul: Lens cleaning: dust, dirt, and water stains noticeably reduce image clarity.
Coverage angle check: cameras can move because of wind, vibration, or changes to the area.
Cable and connection inspection: corrosion and loose connections are common causes of outages.
Recorder and drive check: to confirm normal operation, storage space, and continuous recording.
Review of date, time, and user permission settings.

blocks.p: Emergency repair usually means monitoring stops exactly when you need it, plus the cost of an unplanned call-out. Preventive maintenance catches small issues before they become outages, and spreads the cost across the year.

blocks.tip: Warning signs that need immediate inspection: blurry or shaky images, a camera that does not appear on screen, or recording that stops at unexpected times.

blocks.p: Ideally, maintenance should be scheduled from the first day of installation, with a record for each system showing the date of the last visit and what was done. This makes follow-up easier and improves readiness.
